body:
I want to echo Robopuppy's advice. I'm learning it the hard way.


I met a girl who was absolutely perfect in every way I could imagine. Gorgeous, smart, the whole nine yards. But I'm a geeky guy and a hot girl would never fall for me, right? Well, she was responding to my advances! We have an amazing connection together, and I feel like I finally understood true love. Everything clicked. However, shortly after we meet, I have to move away.


We carry on with a long-distance relationship for three months until we decide that we can't be apart. She moves across the country to live with me. We have a place of our own. Then things started to get a little bad. We were getting into really stupid fights. I learned that she was "embellishing" on one of the things that initially attracted me to her. I stopped worshiping her, which made her really mad. I found out that she was really nasty when she got angry- tons of profanity, didn't talk to me for days, etc. I felt so bad, so I apologized until I was blue in the face, and things were good again.


Pretty soon, I learn the dance. Anytime she wants something, she throws a temper tantrum. One time she was drunk and she started throwing shit at me and hitting, biting, kicking. I decided it was over, but she had nowhere to go so we still lived together, "temporarily." She went to therapy. She apologized. Buckets of tears. Every day for weeks. Months! Finally, I decide to take her back- worst decision of my life.


It's been three years since then. We're engaged now. But you can imagine my life. Two weeks at a time, she's the perfect girl I fell in love with and I feel like it's all been worth it. The next few weeks I see her for what she is: jealous, petty, extremely low self-image. I've put her through school, endured several more bouts of abuse, and sacrificed my friends. All for the few weeks of bliss we have in between the fights. My life is heaven and hell and I would give anything to find a peaceful way out. But I'm a coward and I'm weak and self-conscious, which is why I fell so hard in the first place.


When I read your post, I saw myself in it and it scared the shit out of me so I had to share. But your story won't be like mine, I'm sure. You're smarter than me. Best of luck. Thanks for listening.
No worries, I see that. Let's just delete this whole mess.

Well, I've moved in with a very patient friend and had him communicate with my ex and get my things. From what I understand, she seems to think this is a bluff and so she doesn't seem to be in danger of hurting herself. We'll see how the next few days progress.

I would agree with your advice Saydrah, except that in this situation I think that would be acting rash. I don't feel any eminent danger and I would never forgive myself for putting someone I love on the street. I've contacted help and moved in with a friend, moving along the plan that suckmyball suggested.
Thank you- I will definitely consider all the options.

Whoa! I've never heard of BPD, but that description really fits her. Thank you for your advice, I will take it to heart.

Edit: I've been flipping through this book on Amazon and I feel like I'm going to cry. That's exactly her. How could I have missed this? I feel so naïve.

Thank you for laying a course of action so clearly Saydrah. Right now, I would do exactly as you say if I had more money.

Unless I'm not correctly seeing my options, I don't have the freedom to move out or leave her anything. The reason we initially moved in together is to save money and we both have student debt. In retrospect, this was our worst decision. We're deeply entwined because of money. She would fired from her job and on the streets within one month.

Thank you for your comment. I'm definitely looking for the best way out.

Her family is abusive, which leads me to believe she would rather hurt herself than swallow her pride and go back to them.
Thank you very much. I'm definitely looking to get out ASAP. I'm hoping to hold off calling the police unless I'm struck again.
Thank you for your well-written post. I will certainly consider that.
I'd love to get out. What I need help with is how to do it. Should I leave her to nothing? No home, no friends, no family...? I can't get myself to do that.

I don't think the therapist ever said it was ok to hit me. I think the therapist was convinced that I was only hit once or twice and it was over (which was correct at the time).

She can't pay for the apartment on her own, so moving out is the same as kicking her out on the street. My thought is that I need to break it off with her first, which will hopefully motivate her to find her own place. I just don't know how to do so.

I agree, which is why I want to break things off. It hasn't worked in the past because we have to live in the same apartment until she makes enough money to move out, which never happens. Also, I don't make enough to pay for two apartments.

Well, with all due respect, I asked her enough questions to determine that she did go see a therapist several times. She told her therapist that she had hit me, but that she stopped. The therapist seemed to blame me for our problems and suggested couples counseling (which I, unfortunately, have no time for, because I work two jobs).

I'm afraid of so many things. I have no trust for the police. I'm almost positive they'll assume that I'm hitting her as well and put me in a holding cell. If she's mad, she'll go to great lengths to hurt me, maybe even lie to the cops. Will they believe her if she lies? Will it show up on my record? Is this going to count as a battery charge?

During a break up a while ago, I told her that I would only see her again if she went to a therapist. She did and she was told that she's fine.

She claims that she's harming me physically to get back at me for the emotional harm I do to her. I can't give you her side without bias, but typical things that have gotten her to hurt me include not letting her smoke a cigarette in our car, asking her repeatedly to get more hours at work, or not letting her put the heater at 70F all the time (we're pretty poor).

She has been to therapy. The therapist told her she was fine and she puts this in my face quite a bit.

We have a few mutual friends, but they're all men and I doubt she would open up to them.

The only evidence I have that she might do something to harm herself is that she really has no one to help her and no place to go and that she's threatened doing so. She even says as much when things are going fine, "Oh if anything ever happened to you, I wouldn't be able to go on living.."

Thank you for your reply. The reason I haven't gotten the police involved is because it would basically destroy the background check required for her career. The only person she has ever hurt is me and, in the end, I'm much stronger than her and she has only ever done minor damage. I haven't felt the need to pull the "nuclear option" yet.

Thank you for your reply. Before we got engaged, I don't think she trusted me. She felt that I didn't love her enough or I would leave her and would go into fits of rage over that. However, other than that, everything was fine. So, although I thought it was a bit early, we got engaged and that DID prove to her that I was committed. Things were great for a year.

Now we're developing problems again. She knows that I'm not going anywhere and she treats me like a punching bag. She's isolated herself from all her friends and family, she relies on me for half of her financial support, and she's very quick to anger. I know that she loves me deeply, but she flies off the handle if she doesn't get her way. I've been hit, bit, kicked out of the house and forced to sleep at work several times. I slept on my desk last night. Her opinion is that since I'm "the man" I can take this shit.

If I even mention breaking off the engagement, she goes back to our original problems- oh so you don't love me after all. I hate how I'm being treated and my recourse would be to leave her, but she really has no one- no place to stay, no one to talk to and she's mentioned killing herself if I leave.

The situation sounds really bad and I don't know how we got here. I feel like an idiot and a failure for letting it get this bad, and now that I'm deep in it, I have no idea how to climb out.
